items.summary_short_en: +Anima is a manga about humans with animal transformation abilities, shunned by society.
items.summary__mediumt_en: +Anima is a manga series by Natsumi Mukai about four +Anima—humans with metamorphic animal abilities—who are shunned by society. The story follows Cooro, Husky, Senri, and Nana as they search for others like themselves and a place to belong, encountering friends and foes while learning more about their pasts and their world. The series is set on an island continent divided between Astaria and Sailand, where +Anima are feared and misunderstood due to their powers.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Arcana is a manga by Yua Kotegawa where detective Kensho Murakami investigates serial bombings and encounters Maki, an amnesiac patient who communicates with deceased spirits. As Maki helps Murakami and his partner solve supernatural crimes committed by a mass murderer, Murakami falls for her, only to discover her true nature and connection to Satsuki. The series was serialized in Weekly Young Jump and later adapted into a live-action film.

items.summary__mediumt_en: A.I. Love You by Ken Akamatsu follows Hitoshi Kōbe, a programming prodigy whose AI creation, Thirty, is brought to life by a lightning strike. Hitoshi teaches Thirty about the real world while she helps him navigate relationships. Their lives become complicated when two more of Hitoshi's AIs materialize and a hacker targets Thirty's program. The manga was serialized in Weekly Shōnen Magazine and Magazine Special.

items.summary_short_en: Batman travels to Tokyo to stop a drug that allows users to shapeshift, but it kills them after a day.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Batman: Child of Dreams is a manga by Kia Asamiya where Batman investigates a lethal drug in Tokyo that allows users to shapeshift into anyone they desire for a day before killing them. The drug causes users to transform into twisted versions of Batman villains. Batman, aided by journalist Yuko Yagi, traces the drug to a mutated fan who is the mastermind behind its creation. The series was published in Kodansha's Magazine Z.

items.summary__mediumt_en: I"s is a manga by Masakazu Katsura following shy high schooler Ichitaka Seto's unrequited love for his classmate Iori Yoshizuki. His attempts to confess are repeatedly thwarted by misunderstandings. Complications arise with the return of childhood friend Itsuki Akiba, who had a crush on him. items.summary__mediumt_en: Junk: Record of the Last Hero is a manga by Kia Asamiya. It follows Hiro, a bullied high schooler who receives a powerful Junk super-suit. Initially using it for personal gain and revenge, his actions lead to tragedy. He eventually becomes a hero, protecting others, but struggles with his past. The story explores his maturation, the responsibilities of the Junk system, and its impact on his life and the world.

items.summary__mediumt_en: NOiSE is a manga by Tsutomu Nihei, serving as a prequel to Blame!. It follows police officer Susono Musubi investigating child abductions in a subterranean city. The story reveals information about the Megastructure's origins, its initial size, and the beginnings of Silicon Life. The manga was serialized from 2000 to 2001 and collected into a single volume.

items.summary_short_en: A young girl named Pink steals water from a corrupt company, aided by her robot and lizard friends.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Pink (The Rain Jack Story) is a one-shot manga by Akira Toriyama. It follows Pink, a young girl who acts as a bandit stealing water from the Silver Company during a drought. The company, led by Silver, hires sheriff Cobalt Blue to catch her. Pink, who has a crush on Blue, eventually confronts the company, revealing they imprisoned a rain-maker. The story concludes with a flood after the rain-maker overcompensates.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Yellow is a four-volume yaoi manga by Makoto Tateno. It focuses on the relationship and adventures of Taki and Goh, two elite drug "snatchers" (couriers). Unlike typical boys' love manga, both characters are depicted as equals. Taki is heterosexual, while Goh is homosexual, and the story explores Goh's advances and Taki's reluctance. The title "Yellow" symbolizes the risk in their relationship and job, blending adventure, romance, and high tension.

items.summary_short_en: Asunaro Hakusho is a manga and popular drama about five university friends.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Asunaro Hakusho is a manga by Fumi Saimon, adapted into a highly popular Japanese TV drama. It's a coming-of-age story about five university students who form a close circle of friends. A love triangle develops between Narumi, Tamotsu, and Osamu, leading to tragedy after the accidental death of another friend, Junichiro. Years later, the friends reunite, uncovering surprising secrets. The drama achieved a 31.9% viewer rating, and Takuya Kimura's performance launched his stardom.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Ikkyū is a Japanese manga by Hisashi Sakaguchi, based on the life of the 14th-century Zen monk Ikkyū. Serialized from 1993 to 1995, it was left unfinished due to the author's death. The manga depicts Ikkyū's spiritual struggles and transformation into an unorthodox, wandering monk during the Muromachi period, blending historical facts with fiction and Noh theatre influences.

items.summary__mediumt_en: King of Thorn is a Japanese manga by Yuji Iwahara. It follows Kasumi Ishiki and other survivors who are awakened from suspended animation to find a world overrun by monstrous creatures after a plague turns people to stone. They were part of an experiment by Venus Gate to cure the "Medusa virus." The survivors must navigate the dangerous ruins and uncover the truth behind the virus and the dramatic changes to their environment.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Okami-san is a manga by Ichimaru following Hatsuko Yamazaki, who becomes the manageress of a sumo stable after marrying a wrestler. items.summary__mediumt_en: Otaku no Musume-san by Stu-Hiro follows Kouta Morisaki, a 26-year-old otaku, whose life changes when a young girl, Kanau Yukimura, appears claiming to be his daughter. items.summary__mediumt_en: Gingitsune by Sayori Ochiai follows Makoto Saeki, the daughter of a shrine priest, who possesses 'The Sight' allowing her to see shrine heralds. She befriends Gintarou, a fox messenger, and together they act as intermediaries between gods and humans, helping those who visit their Inari shrine. The series depicts their everyday lives and the supernatural elements intertwined with human affairs. An anime adaptation was also broadcast.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Kuso Miso Technique is a one-shot gay manga by Junichi Yamakawa depicting a sexual encounter between Masaki Michishita and Takakazu Abe in a public restroom. The encounter involves various sexual acts and complications, including the need to urinate and defecate. Originally published in 1987, it gained notoriety as an internet meme in the early 2000s. It has been adapted into a live-action film and an upcoming anime film.

items.summary_short_en: Lion Books is a manga series by Osamu Tezuka, published in the 1950s and 1970s. Partially adapted into an anime.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Lion Books is a Japanese manga series by Osamu Tezuka, published by Shueisha. It includes stories from the 1950s and 1970s, with no continuations between them. Two stories were adapted into an experimental anime series, the Lion Books Collection, in the 1980s and 1990s. "The Green Cat" (1983) was an early OVA attempt, and "Adachi-ga Hara" (1991) was released theatrically. The series is available on DVD and streaming services.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Parallel is a shōnen manga by Toshihiko Kobayashi. It follows Shinnosuke Nekota and Sakura Hoshino, who must live together after their parents become unofficially engaged and leave the country. The manga explores their developing relationship amidst school life and supporting characters, culminating in them starting their own romantic relationship when their parents' engagement is called off.

items.summary_short_en: Tears of a Lamb is a manga about an anorexic girl trying to help her brother's amnesiac friend recover his memory.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Tears of a Lamb is a manga series by Banri Hidaka. It centers on Kei Hasumi, an anorexic teenager in love with her brother's friend, Kakeru Suwa, who has lost his memory. Kei searches for a ring given to his girlfriend to aid his recovery, with help from classmate Kyosuke Kanzaki. The series was serialized in Hana to Yume and licensed for English release by CMX Manga. It also had drama CDs and an illustration collection.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Futari Daka is a Japanese motorcycle racing manga by Kaoru Shintani, focusing on the rivalry between Sawatari Taka and Toujou Taka. Both named 'Taka' (hawk/falcon), they compete fiercely on the track. The manga won the 1984 Shogakukan Manga Award. It was adapted into a 36-episode anime series broadcast on Fuji TV and later in France. The anime was the last to be animated by Kokusai Eiga-sha.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Lion Books is a manga series by Osamu Tezuka, published in the 1950s and 1970s. Two stories, "The Green Cat" and "Adachi-ga Hara," were adapted into an experimental anime series called the Lion Books Collection. "The Green Cat" was an early OVA attempt, while "Adachi-ga Hara" received a theatrical release. The series was later re-released on DVD.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Itazura na Kiss follows Kotoko Aihara, a clumsy high school girl who confesses to the brilliant Naoki Irie, only to be rejected. The manga, by Kaoru Tada, was unfinished due to the author's death but remains popular, with multiple adaptations.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Alien Nine is a manga series where students at Elementary School No. 9 join the "Alien Party" to capture aliens using symbiotic Borgs. The teacher, Megumi Hisakawa, secretly releases aliens for training. Protagonist Yuri Otani struggles with fear, while her friends Kasumi and Kumi face increasingly dangerous alien encounters, leading to tragic events and betrayals.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Excel Saga is a manga series by Kōshi Rikudō about the secret organization Across's attempts to conquer Fukuoka as a first step towards world domination. The series follows Excel, a key member of Across, and the city's defense by Dr. Kabapu's agency. An anime adaptation by Victor Entertainment aired in 1999, known for its experimental animation and an unaired finale. The series blends parody and in-jokes, with characters and locations derived from Fukuoka.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Ēldlive is a manga by Akira Amano about Chūta Kokonose, a middle school boy who can hear a voice no one else can. He's recruited into the space police, ēlDLIVE, and discovers the voice belongs to an alien named Dolugh living inside him. items.summary__mediumt_en: The manga Cat's Eye by Tsukasa Hojo follows the three Kisugi sisters—Hitomi, Rui, and Ai—who lead a double life as art thieves. They steal artworks belonging to their missing father, Michael Heinz. Hitomi's fiancé, Toshio Utsumi, is a police officer investigating the Cat's Eye case, unaware of their identity. The series has been adapted into anime, live-action films, and a French TV series, with a crossover ONA with Lupin III and a new ONA adaptation planned.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Children of the Whales is a manga by Abi Umeda about Chakuro, a boy living on a giant vessel called the Mud Whale. Society is divided into the Marked, who use psychic "thymia" at the cost of lifespan, and the Unmarked. items.summary__mediumt_en: Haré+Guu is a manga by Renjuro Kindaichi about Haré, a ten-year-old boy living in the jungle with his lazy mother, Weda. Her feelings are complicated by Ren's existing relationship with Mayuka Korenaga. Ninako also navigates her friendship with Daiki Korenaga and the affections of his friend Takumi Ando. items.summary__mediumt_en: Tuxedo Gin by Tokihiko Matsuura is about Ginji Kusanagi, a high school boxer killed before his first date. He is reincarnated as a penguin to be near his crush, Minako Sasebo. Living as her pet penguin, Gin-chan, he protects her from rivals. items.summary__mediumt_en: Delicious! is a manga by Yui Ayumi and Miyuki Kobayashi. It follows Ringo Nonohara, who dreams of stardom and tries out for a cooking show. Despite her lack of cooking skills, she gets the lead role with help from her neighbor, chef Kazuomi Tsutsui. The series details Ringo's journey to achieve her dream, navigating challenges and relationships along the way. Each part of the manga includes a recipe for readers.

items.summary__mediumt_en: The Heart of Thomas is a 1974 manga by Moto Hagio, set in a German boys' gymnasium after student Thomas Werner's suicide. His classmate Juli Bauernfeind receives a suicide letter and grapples with guilt. The arrival of Erich Frühling, who resembles Thomas, complicates matters. The series explores themes of unrequited love, trauma, and friendship, and is considered an early work of shōnen-ai.

items.summary__mediumt_en: No. 5 is a manga series written and illustrated by Taiyō Matsumoto. It was serialized in Shogakukan's seinen manga magazine Monthly Ikki from November 2000 to January 2005. The series was compiled into eight volumes. Viz Media initially released the series in North America but discontinued it due to low sales, later re-publishing it in an omnibus edition. It was recognized at the 7th Japan Media Arts Festival.

items.summary__mediumt_en: New York New York by Marimo Ragawa is a shojo manga focusing on the relationship between closeted gay NYPD officer Cain Walker and barista Mel Fredericks. Serialized from 1995-1998, it explores their tumultuous relationship and challenges including sexual assault, marriage, parenting, and HIV/AIDS. The series is noted for its realistic depiction of gay identity and social issues within the yaoi genre.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Handsome na Kanojo is a romantic-comedy manga by Wataru Yoshizumi, serialized from 1988-1992. It follows 14-year-old actress Mio Hagiwara and aspiring director Ichiya Kumagai. Initially finding each other annoying, they develop feelings and become a couple while pursuing their dreams. The series also includes Yoshizumi's debut manga, "Radical Romance," and features crossovers with her later work, Marmalade Boy.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Blue Period by Tsubasa Yamaguchi follows Yatora Yaguchi, a popular student who feels empty. Inspired by a striking Shibuya scene, he discovers art and aspires to attend the prestigious Tokyo University of the Arts. The manga details his challenging journey to master painting and pass the difficult entrance exams, exploring themes of passion and self-discovery.

items.summary_short_en: A 19th-century Paris manga about Vanitas and vampire Noé healing cursed vampires with a grimoire.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Set in 19th-century Paris, Jun Mochizuki's "The Case Study of Vanitas" follows human Vanitas and vampire Noé Archiviste. Vanitas uses "The Book of Vanitas" to heal vampires afflicted by the malnomen, a curse causing predatory behavior. They face a mysterious threat called Charlatan, potentially corrupting the sick vampires. The manga, serialized since 2015, was adapted into an anime by Bones. It's praised for character handling, action, and comedy.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Sekai de Ichiban Yasashii Ongaku, meaning 'The World's Most Tender Music,' is a Japanese manga series by Mari Ozawa. It was serialized in Kodansha's Kiss magazine from 1993 to 1999 and collected into 16 volumes. The series won the 19th Kodansha Manga Award for shōjo manga. In 1996, it was adapted into a two-episode live-action television drama.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Eight Clouds Rising (Yakumo Tatsu) is a shōjo manga by Natsumi Itsuki. It follows Kuraki Fuzuchi, a young man with psychic powers and sword skills, and college student Takeo Nanachi, who also possesses similar abilities. items.summary_short_en: Manga about Hitler's life by Shigeru Mizuki, published in English by Drawn & Quarterly in 2015.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Shigeru Mizuki's Hitler is a manga depicting Adolf Hitler's life, serialized starting in 1971. The English translation, released in 2015, was adapted from a French version. Critics note Hitler is portrayed as he was and as he saw himself, often appearing "dopey, sad, and often pathetic." The manga uses Mizuki's signature style of cartoon characters in detailed settings. The Holocaust is referenced at the beginning and end, serving as bookends to the narrative.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Shout Out Loud! is a yaoi manga series by Satosumi Takaguchi. It follows Shino Hisae, a 35-year-old voice actor who looks like a teenager, and his 17-year-old son, Nakaya, who is discovering his homosexuality. Shino deals with advances from coworkers while Nakaya navigates his own identity and a false pregnancy scare. The series explores themes of sexuality and family relationships, with less explicit content until later volumes.

items.summary_short_en: Manga and anime series about a boy who travels through time with ghosts from WWII.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Natsu no Arashi! is a manga by Jin Kobayashi adapted into an anime series. It follows 13-year-old Yasaka, who meets Arashi, a 16-year-old ghost from WWII with time-traveling powers. They form a connection, allowing them to travel back in time to rescue people from air raids. The plot expands with the appearance of Kaja, another ghost from Arashi's time, and Jun, a girl who disguises herself as a boy and travels with Kaja.

items.title: 夢みるエンジェルブルー

items.title: 夢みる太陽

items.title: 夢みる惑星

items.title: 夢をかなえる爆笑! 日本美術マンガ おしえて北斎!

items.title: 夢をみたいの

items.title: 夢使い
items.summary_short: 植芝理一原作の漫画で、2001年に『月刊アフタヌーン』で連載開始、後に2006年にアニメ化された作品。
items.summary_short_en: Manga and anime about 'dream masters' who turn nightmares into peaceful dreams.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Yume Tsukai is a manga and anime series about 'dream masters' who transform nightmares into peaceful dreams. They search for escaped nightmares that manifest in the real world as paranormal phenomena. The dream masters defeat these nightmares and return them to their owners. The anime features haunting music and transformed children's toys, while the manga offers more in-depth cases and explores scenarios beyond just nightmares.

items.title: 夢喰いメリー
items.summary_short: 牛木義隆のオリジナル長編4コマ漫画で、2008年に連載開始し、2011年にテレビアニメ化された作品。
items.summary_short_en: Manga and anime where a boy helps a dream demon return to her world.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Dream Eater Merry is a manga and anime series about Yumeji Fujiwara, who can see the aura of dreams, and Merry Nightmare, a dream demon seeking to return home. Yumeji helps Merry, and together they fight evil dream demons who possess humans to create an army. After defeating Pharos Hercules, Merry's quest continues, and they investigate new dream demon manifestations. It's revealed Yumeji and Merry met 10 years prior.

items.title: 夢幻の如く

items.summary__mediumt_en: High school girl Minako Ifu attracts the attention of the demon Deimos, who believes she is the reincarnation of his twin sister and lover, Venus. Deimos seeks to bring Minako to the underworld so Venus can possess her body. The series explores Deimos's pursuit, his conflicted feelings for Minako, and his destructive path.

items.title: 日本の漫画
items.summary_short: 日本の漫画は19世紀初頭の北斎漫画に始まり、以降世界的な文化・産業となった。
items.summary_short_en: Manga are Japanese comics or graphic novels with a long history, popular across all ages and genres.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Manga are comics or graphic novels originating from Japan, characterized by a style developed in the late 19th century. They encompass a wide range of genres and are enjoyed by people of all ages in Japan. The manga market has seen significant growth, especially in digital formats, and has gained a substantial worldwide readership, with Japanese publishers now among the top globally. Manga are typically printed in black-and-white and serialized in magazines before being collected into volumes.

items.summary_short_en: Haguregumo is a manga series about Cloud, a womanizing samurai who avoids work, set in Edo period Japan.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Haguregumo is a Japanese manga series by George Akiyama, serialized from 1973 to 2017. Set in the late Edo period, it follows the life of Cloud, a notorious womanizer who neglects work. The story focuses on his family, including his wife Turtle and their children, who often join him in his idle pursuits. The series has been adapted into multiple television dramas and an anime film.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Clean Freak! Aoyama-kun is a Japanese manga series by Taku Sakamoto. It centers on Aoyama, a first-year high school student and a genius soccer player with severe mysophobia, making him obsessed with cleanliness. His unique playing style involves extreme caution to avoid physical contact. The series follows his high school life, soccer club activities, and interactions with teammates and rivals, including Kaoru Zaizen and Moka Gotō. An anime adaptation aired in 2017.

items.summary_short_en: Blade of the Immortal is a manga about a cursed samurai seeking redemption by killing 1,000 evil men.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Blade of the Immortal is a Japanese manga series by Hiroaki Samura, set in the mid-Tokugawa Shogunate period. It follows Manji, a skilled rōnin cursed with immortality by sacred bloodworms. To regain his mortality, Manji vows to kill 1,000 evil men. He allies with Rin Asano, whose parents were murdered by Anotsu Kagehisa, the leader of the rogue swordsmen group Ittō-ryū. The series explores themes of redemption, violence, and morality, and has been adapted into anime and live-action films.

items.summary_short_en: Beyond Twilight is a manga about Ritsu, who inherits the ability to see spirits and forms a contract with a demon.
items.summary__mediumt_en: Beyond Twilight is a Japanese manga series by Ichiko Ima. It follows Ritsu, a young man who inherits the ability to see spirits and demons from his novelist grandfather. This "sixth sense" makes him vulnerable to supernatural forces. After his grandfather's death, Ritsu forms a contract with a demon guardian named Blue Storm. The series consists of largely self-contained stories focusing on supernatural incidents involving Ritsu and Blue Storm. It has been adapted into a television drama, drama CDs, and stage plays.

items.summary_short_en: Moto Hagio's "The Heart of Thomas" (1974) is an early shōnen-ai manga.
items.summary__mediumt_en: The Heart of Thomas is a 1974 Japanese manga series by Moto Hagio, serialized in Shūkan Shōjo Comic. Inspired by Hermann Hesse and the Bildungsroman genre, it follows events at a German boys' gymnasium after a student's suicide. It is considered an early work of shōnen-ai. The series significantly influenced shōjo manga and has been adapted into a film, stage play, and novel. An English translation was published in 2013.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Weed, or Ginga Densetsu Weed, is a Japanese manga series by Yoshihiro Takahashi, serving as a sequel to his "Silver Fang." It follows Weed, the son of the original protagonist Gin, as he searches for his father and protects the Ōu Mountains. The manga was serialized from 1999 to 2009, with 60 volumes published. items.summary__mediumt_en: Lion Books is a Japanese manga series by Osamu Tezuka, published by Shueisha. Two stories, "The Green Cat" (1983) and "Adachi-ga Hara" (1991), were adapted into an experimental anime series called the Lion Books Collection. "The Green Cat" is noted as an early attempt at an original video animation (OVA). "Adachi-ga Hara" was the only film released theatrically. The series was re-released on DVD in 2003.

items.summary__mediumt_en: Sweet Blue Flowers is a Japanese yuri manga series by Takako Shimura, serialized from 2004 to 2013. It follows Fumi Manjōme, a lesbian high school girl, and her childhood friend Akira Okudaira. The story explores their relationships and personal growth. An 11-episode anime television series aired in 2009. The manga was licensed in North America by Viz Media, and the anime by Right Stuf Inc.
